question: What is the primary function of the immune system in the human body?

options.A: Pumping oxygenated blood to body tissues
options.B: Regulating hormonal balance and metabolic rate
options.C: Filtering waste products from the bloodstream
options.D: Protecting the body against foreign pathogens

explanation: The main role of the immune system is to defend the body against harmful invaders like bacteria and viruses. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h1)

question: What happens when the immune system fails to distinguish between self and non-self cells?

options.A: Red blood cells immediately stop carrying oxygen
options.B: Physical barriers like skin become completely dry
options.C: The body develops an autoimmune disorder
options.D: Pathogens multiply without any cellular resistance

explanation: An inability to recognize self-tissues leads the immune system to mistakenly attack healthy body cells. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h1)

question: Which type of immunity is present from birth and acts as a non-specific defense?
explanation: Innate immunity is our inborn, general defense system that reacts the same way to all invaders. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h2)

question: What key feature distinguishes adaptive immunity from innate immunity?

options.B: Absence of any white blood cell involvement
options.D: Reliance solely on intact skin and mucous layers

explanation: Adaptive immunity tailors its response to specific pathogens and remembers them for faster future protection. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h2)

question: Where do T-lymphocytes primarily mature before entering circulation?
explanation: T-cells are produced in the bone marrow but travel to the thymus gland to complete their maturation. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h3)

question: What is the primary role of B-lymphocytes in the immune response?

options.B: Acting as the first physical barrier in the skin
options.C: Differentiating into plasma cells to produce antibodies
options.D: Filtering dead red blood cells from the bloodstream

explanation: B-cells transform into plasma factories that secrete specific antibodies to target circulating antigens. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h3)

question: What is an antigen?

options.A: A physical barrier located on the surface of skin
options.B: A protective protein produced by mature plasma cells
options.C: A specialized white blood cell found in lymph nodes
options.D: A foreign substance that triggers an immune response

explanation: Antigens are molecules on pathogens that the body identifies as foreign and reacts against. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h4)

question: Why is the secondary immune response much faster than the primary response?

options.A: Memory cells recognize the familiar antigen immediately
options.B: Antibodies are permanently stored inside red blood cells
options.C: The physical skin barriers are thicker after the first infection
options.D: Pathogens become weaker upon entering the body a second time

explanation: Memory B and T cells left from the first exposure allow the immune system to react instantly. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h4)

question: Which chemical mediator is released during tissue injury to cause vasodilation?
explanation: Mast cells release histamine, which dilates blood vessels and increases permeability at the injury site. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of increased capillary permeability during acute inflammation?

options.A: Cooling down the affected body part to prevent fever
options.B: Stopping blood flow completely to starve out local bacteria
options.C: Preventing red blood cells from escaping the circulation
options.D: Allowing white blood cells to reach the injured tissue

explanation: Permeable capillaries let immune cells and protective proteins exit the blood and enter the damaged area. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of administering a routine vaccination?

options.A: Providing immediate short-term antibodies from donor serum
options.B: Stimulating memory cell production without causing disease
options.C: Destroying all resident bacteria living on the human skin
options.D: Curing an active chronic infection currently in progress

explanation: Vaccines safely train the immune system to recognize pathogens by producing memory cells ahead of real exposure. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h6)

question: What does herd immunity achieve within a population?

options.A: Ensuring that every single citizen receives an annual booster shot
options.B: Eliminating the need for sterile equipment during minor surgeries
options.C: Preventing bacteria from ever mutating inside human hosts
options.D: Protecting vulnerable unvaccinated people through high community immunity

explanation: High vaccination rates in a community reduce disease spread, indirectly shielding those who cannot take vaccines. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h6)

question: Which type of hypersensitivity reaction involves immediate IgE-mediated allergic responses?
explanation: Type I hypersensitivity is an immediate allergic reaction driven by IgE antibody binding and mast cell degranulation. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h7)

question: What characterizes an autoimmune disease?

options.A: The immune system attacks the body's own healthy tissues
options.B: The body completely lacks any circulating white blood cells
options.C: Pathogens hide inside bone marrow and evade all antibodies
options.D: An allergic reaction occurs only after touching certain metals

explanation: Autoimmunity happens when immune tolerance fails, leading to destructive attacks against self-antigens. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h7)

question: Which nursing intervention is essential when caring for a severely neutropenic patient?

options.A: Implementing strict protective isolation and hand hygiene
options.B: Withholding all prescribed prophylactic antibiotic medications
options.C: Allowing visitors to bring fresh flowers into the hospital room
options.D: Encouraging the consumption of fresh raw fruits and salads

explanation: Protective precautions shield vulnerable patients from acquiring dangerous environmental pathogens. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h8)

question: A patient with low neutrophil counts shows no obvious swelling or pus at a surgical site. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: The suppressed immune system cannot mount a typical inflammatory response
options.B: Bacteria cannot multiply in patients who have low white blood cells
options.C: Antibiotics are actively blocking the formation of local pain receptors
options.D: The surgical wound has healed completely without any cellular help

explanation: Neutropenic patients often fail to display classic signs of infection like pus or marked swelling because they lack white blood cells. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T14#GNS111_U2_T14_h8)
